item.content:encoded:
Victoria’s Secret and PINK offer early talent opportunities designed to help students gain practical experience and begin building careers in the specialty retail industry.

The programme is aimed at the next generation of associates who bring fresh perspectives, imagination, passion and energy to the workplace. Through its internship opportunities, Victoria’s Secret and PINK seek to develop students and early-career talent by providing meaningful experiences that can serve as a foundation for future professional success.

For students interested in retail, fashion, business and related career paths, these internship opportunities can provide an opportunity to gain exposure to a major specialty retail environment while developing professional skills.

About the Victoria’s Secret and PINK Early Talent Opportunities

Victoria’s Secret and PINK describe their early talent opportunities as an important part of developing the next generation of associates.

The programme recognizes that the future of the company depends on attracting students and emerging professionals who can bring new ideas and perspectives to the organization.

The company emphasizes:

  • Fresh perspectives
  • Imagination and creativity
  • Energy and enthusiasm
  • Passion for specialty retail
  • Professional development
  • Meaningful student opportunities

The objective is not simply to provide students with short-term work experience. The early talent programme is positioned as a way to help develop associates and prepare them for future success within the business.

Internship Opportunities at Victoria’s Secret and PINK

The internship programme provides students with an opportunity to gain practical exposure to the company and its operations.

An internship can be an important step for students who want to understand how a large specialty retail business operates while developing skills that can support their future careers.

Victoria’s Secret and PINK describe an early talent opportunity as a place where students can begin developing themselves professionally and potentially build a foundation for a long-term career.

What Students Can Expect

The internship programme is designed around professional development and exposure to the business.

Students considering an internship should expect an environment focused on helping early-career associates develop their capabilities and gain experience.

The company’s early talent approach emphasizes developing associates to become highly capable professionals within the specialty retail industry.

This makes the opportunity potentially valuable for students who want to combine their academic background with practical workplace experience.

Internship Qualifications

Victoria’s Secret and PINK provide specific information about internship qualifications through their official internship information.

Applicants should review the qualification requirements carefully before applying to determine whether they meet the requirements for the particular internship opportunity they are interested in.

Because internship requirements can vary depending on the position, students should not assume that every internship has identical eligibility criteria.

Applicants should therefore review:

  1. The specific internship position.
  2. The listed qualifications.
  3. Any academic requirements.
  4. Any experience requirements.
  5. Any other requirements included in the individual vacancy.
  6. The location and working arrangements associated with the position.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The early talent programme is particularly relevant to students and individuals at the beginning of their professional careers who are interested in specialty retail.

Students who are passionate about the retail industry and want to bring creative ideas and fresh perspectives to a company may find these opportunities particularly relevant.

Potential applicants may come from a range of academic and professional backgrounds depending on the specific internship available.

However, candidates should always check the requirements of the individual internship before submitting an application.

APPLY HERE

Why Consider an Internship With Victoria’s Secret and PINK?

An internship can provide more than an entry on a CV. It can help students understand how their academic knowledge translates into a professional environment.

Potential areas of development include:

  • Professional workplace experience
  • Exposure to specialty retail
  • Collaboration and teamwork
  • Understanding business operations
  • Professional communication
  • Problem-solving
  • Creative thinking
  • Development of industry knowledge
  • Building a professional foundation

The company’s stated approach is focused on developing associates and helping early talent become future success stories.

Early Talent and Career Development

One of the central ideas behind the programme is the development of future associates.

Victoria’s Secret and PINK state that they aim to develop their associates into highly capable professionals within the industry.

For students, this means an internship can represent an opportunity to begin understanding the company’s working environment while developing skills and experience that can contribute to their longer-term career development.

Students should therefore approach the internship not simply as a temporary position, but as an opportunity to learn, contribute and develop professionally.

How to Apply

Students interested in Victoria’s Secret and PINK internship opportunities should review the company’s official internship information and available vacancies.

The official internship page provides information covering:

  • What to expect from an internship
  • Internship qualifications
  • How to apply
  • What happens after submitting an application

Applicants should carefully read the relevant information before submitting an application.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Victoria’s Secret & PINK Early Talent Internship Opportunities

Official Internship Information:
Victoria’s Secret & PINK Internship Opportunities

What Happens After You Apply?

Victoria’s Secret and PINK also provide information explaining what applicants can expect after submitting an internship application.

Applicants should review the official process so they understand the next steps following their submission.

The application process may vary depending on the specific internship or position, so candidates should rely on the information provided for the vacancy they are applying for.

Application Deadline

The information provided does not state a specific deadline for the Victoria’s Secret and PINK internship programme.

Because individual internship vacancies may have different closing dates or availability periods, applicants should check the specific internship listing for the position they want to apply for.

Students interested in these opportunities are encouraged not to delay their applications, particularly when a specific vacancy is currently available.

Important Things to Check Before Applying

Before applying for an internship, prospective candidates should make sure they understand the specific position.

It is important to check:

  • The internship title
  • Location
  • Academic requirements
  • Eligibility requirements
  • Required skills
  • Application instructions
  • Application closing date, if provided
  • Any additional requirements listed in the vacancy

This will help applicants determine whether the particular opportunity matches their academic background and career goals.

Conclusion

The Victoria’s Secret and PINK Early Talent Opportunities provide students with a pathway to gain practical professional experience while exploring careers within the specialty retail industry.

The programme is built around the idea of developing the next generation of associates and giving students meaningful opportunities to become future professionals.

For students passionate about specialty retail and those who can bring fresh perspectives, creativity, imagination and energy to the workplace, an internship can provide valuable exposure to a major retail environment and help establish a strong foundation for future career development.

There is no specific overall deadline stated in the information provided, so students should regularly review the official internship page and individual vacancy listings for currently available opportunities and their respective application deadlines.

item.content:encoded:
The Goethe-Institut International Coproduction Fund (IKF) supports international artistic collaborations that bring creators from different cultural backgrounds together to develop innovative productions and new approaches to intercultural exchange.

The fund is designed to encourage international coproduction, cultural dialogue, artistic collaboration and the development of new creative networks within a global context.

The 2026 application period for the current funding round runs from 17 August to 12 October 2026.

About the International Coproduction Fund

The International Coproduction Fund supports collaborative projects involving international partners, with a particular focus on productions that encourage meaningful cultural exchange.

The fund aims to create opportunities for artists and cultural practitioners to work across borders, exchange ideas and develop innovative artistic projects together.

Supported areas include:

  • Music
  • Dance and theatre

The programme encourages applicants to develop projects that demonstrate genuine international collaboration rather than simply presenting an existing production in another country.

What the Fund Supports

The International Coproduction Fund focuses on international coproductions that demonstrate partnership-based and dialogue-oriented approaches.

Projects should contribute to:

  • International cultural exchange
  • Collaboration between artists and cultural practitioners
  • Development of new artistic networks
  • Innovative production methods
  • Intercultural dialogue
  • New approaches to international artistic cooperation

Applicants are encouraged to demonstrate how their proposed project will benefit from the collaboration between international partners and how the partnership will contribute to the artistic development of the production.

2026 Application Round

From 2026, the Goethe-Institut has confirmed two application periods.

The second application round runs from mid-August until 12 October 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Projects submitted during this round should be scheduled to:

  • Start: January 2027
  • End: 31 December 2027

Applicants are encouraged to regularly check the Goethe-Institut website for any updates concerning the application process and requirements.

APPLY HERE

Inclusion and Accessibility

The Goethe-Institut is committed to making cultural activities accessible to people with disabilities and strongly encourages artists with disabilities to apply.

Accessibility-related costs connected to eligible projects will be covered by the fund.

This provides an important opportunity for applicants to incorporate accessibility considerations into their project planning without having to treat accessibility costs as an additional barrier to participation.

Sustainability

The International Coproduction Fund also places importance on sustainability.

Applicants are encouraged to consider how their projects can be planned and delivered in an environmentally responsible way.

The Goethe-Institut can provide advice to applicants on how to incorporate environmentally friendly approaches into their projects.

Application Deadline

The deadline for the second 2026 application round is:

12 October 2026 at 23:59 CET

Projects submitted during this round should begin from January 2027 and run through 31 December 2027.

Visit HERE to learn more about the International Coproduction Fund (IKF) 2026

Contact

For questions concerning the International Coproduction Fund, applicants can contact:

Goethe-Institut e.V.
International Coproduction Fund (IKF)
Email: koproduktionsfonds@goethe.de

Conclusion

The International Coproduction Fund (IKF) provides an opportunity for artists and cultural practitioners to develop international music, dance and theatre productions through meaningful cross-border collaboration.

The programme places particular emphasis on international cultural exchange, innovative artistic production, intercultural cooperation and the creation of new networks.

Applicants interested in developing collaborative artistic projects for 2027 should review the fund’s requirements carefully and submit their applications before the 12 October 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF) is inviting expressions of interest and nominations from suitably qualified individuals who may be considered for appointment to its Board of Directors. The opportunity provides individuals with an interest and experience in conservation, biodiversity protection, sustainable development and regional environmental governance with an opportunity to contribute to the strategic direction of an important Caribbean environmental fund.

The proposed Board appointment will run for a maximum of two years, with the proposed term beginning on 1 October 2026.

Applications and nominations must be submitted by 7 September 2026.

About the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund

The Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF) is a regional environmental fund established to provide stable, long-term financial resources for conservation, ecosystem-based adaptation and biodiversity protection across the Caribbean.

The Fund plays a role in supporting long-term approaches to environmental conservation and sustainable development throughout the region. Its work involves the mobilization and management of financial resources intended to support biodiversity and ecosystem-related priorities.

As a regional institution handling resources for environmental and conservation purposes, effective governance and oversight are important to ensuring that the Fund operates responsibly and achieves meaningful strategic impact.

It is within this context that the CBF Governance Committee has opened a formal call for individuals who may be considered for vacant positions on its skills-based Board of Directors.

CBF Board of Directors Opportunity

The CBF is seeking expressions of interest and nominations from suitably qualified individuals for possible appointment to its Board of Directors.

The Board is described as skills-based, meaning that the selection process is intended to identify individuals whose knowledge, experience and professional capabilities can contribute to the governance and strategic oversight of the Fund.

The appointment is proposed for a maximum period of:

  • Two years
  • Proposed start date: 1 October 2026
  • Application deadline: 7 September 2026

The opportunity is therefore intended for individuals who are interested in contributing at a governance and strategic level to a regional organization focused on biodiversity conservation and environmental financing.

Why Serve on the CBF Board?

Serving on the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund Board provides an opportunity to contribute directly to the governance and strategic development of a regional institution working on biodiversity and conservation.

According to the opportunity announcement, Board members can contribute to several important areas.

1. Help Shape the Strategic Direction of the CBF

Directors will have an opportunity to contribute to the strategic direction of the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund.

Board-level participation can therefore involve contributing perspectives and expertise that help guide the institution’s priorities and long-term development.

The Board plays an important role in ensuring that the Fund continues to develop in a way that supports its conservation and biodiversity objectives.

2. Support Strong Governance

The CBF is seeking Board members as part of efforts to ensure:

  • Robust fiduciary oversight
  • Objective governance
  • Strategic impact

This makes Board participation particularly important because the Fund is responsible for managing resources intended to support environmental and conservation priorities.

Directors can contribute to the governance structures and oversight needed to support responsible institutional decision-making.

3. Contribute to Regional Conservation

The CBF’s work is focused on conservation, ecosystem-based adaptation and biodiversity protection across the Caribbean.

Board members therefore have the opportunity to contribute to an institution whose activities are connected to some of the region’s broader environmental priorities.

The position provides an opportunity to support efforts aimed at protecting biodiversity and strengthening long-term financing for conservation.

4. Engage With Regional and International Partners

Board service can also provide opportunities for Directors to engage with partners working in conservation and sustainable development.

The announcement notes that Directors may have opportunities to represent the CBF at:

  • Regional meetings
  • International meetings
  • Convenings
  • Other strategic engagements

Where appropriate, these engagements may also involve travel.

This can provide Board members with opportunities to participate in discussions involving Caribbean and international partners committed to conservation and sustainable development.

Nature of the Board Appointment

The CBF Board opportunity is different from a conventional employment position.

Board service is voluntary and does not carry remuneration.

This means individuals appointed to the Board should understand that they will not receive a salary or regular remuneration for their Board service.

However, Directors may have opportunities to represent the CBF through regional and international engagements, including meetings and other strategic activities.

The announcement specifically notes that travel may be involved where appropriate.

Appointment Term

The proposed appointment is for a maximum of two years.

The proposed commencement date is:

1 October 2026

Applicants should therefore be prepared for the possibility of serving on the Board during the proposed two-year period, subject to the terms and conditions of the appointment.

Who Is This Opportunity For?

The CBF is specifically seeking suitably qualified individuals who may be considered for vacant positions on its skills-based Board of Directors.

The announcement emphasizes that the Board is skills-based, indicating that professional knowledge, expertise and relevant capabilities are important considerations.

However, the information provided in the announcement does not specify a detailed list of educational qualifications, years of professional experience, specific professional disciplines or individual technical skills required from applicants.

Therefore, applicants should carefully review the official application materials and nomination process for any additional requirements that may apply.

Geographic Eligibility

The Caribbean Biodiversity Fund is a regional Caribbean environmental fund, and the Board opportunity is connected to its work across the Caribbean.

However, the supplied announcement does not explicitly state a nationality restriction or provide a specific list of countries from which applicants must come.

It also does not provide a specific race or ethnicity requirement.

Applicants should therefore refer to the official CBF application materials for any additional geographic or eligibility requirements that may apply.

Application Deadline

The deadline for submitting an expression of interest or nomination is:

7 September 2026

Interested individuals should ensure that their applications or nominations are submitted before the stated deadline.

Because the opportunity is for Board-level service and the appointment is proposed to begin on 1 October 2026, interested candidates should allow sufficient time to review the requirements and prepare their submission.

APPLY HERE

Proposed Start Date

The proposed start date for the Board appointment is:

1 October 2026

The appointment is expected to run for a maximum of two years.

How to Apply

Individuals interested in being considered for the CBF Board of Directors should submit their expression of interest or nomination through the official application process.

Application deadline: 7 September 2026

Apply Now:
CBF Board of Directors Expression of Interest Application

Applicants should carefully review the official application form and provide the information requested as part of the expression-of-interest or nomination process.

Important Information for Potential Applicants

Before applying, candidates should understand several important aspects of the opportunity:

  1. It is a Board appointment opportunity, rather than a conventional employment vacancy.
  2. The appointment is proposed for a maximum of two years.
  3. The proposed start date is 1 October 2026.
  4. Board service is voluntary and unpaid.
  5. Directors may have opportunities to participate in regional and international meetings and strategic engagements.
  6. Travel may be involved where appropriate.
  7. The Board is described as skills-based.
  8. The CBF is seeking individuals who are suitably qualified to contribute to the governance and strategic direction of the Fund.
  9. The application deadline is 7 September 2026.
  10. The supplied announcement does not provide a detailed list of qualifications, professional experience requirements or nationality restrictions, so applicants should consult the official application materials for further information.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund Board of Directors 2026

About the CBF’s Governance Priorities

The call for Board members is closely connected to the CBF’s need for strong institutional governance.

The Fund was established to provide long-term financial resources for:

  • Conservation
  • Ecosystem-based adaptation
  • Biodiversity protection

Because these areas involve significant regional environmental priorities, the Board has an important role in supporting responsible governance and strategic decision-making.

The CBF Governance Committee is therefore seeking individuals who can potentially strengthen the Board’s collective skills and contribute to its fiduciary oversight, objective governance and strategic impact.

Conclusion

The Caribbean Biodiversity Fund Board of Directors Call for Expressions of Interest presents an opportunity for suitably qualified individuals to contribute to the governance and strategic direction of a regional institution dedicated to conservation, ecosystem-based adaptation and biodiversity protection across the Caribbean.

The proposed Board term is up to two years, beginning on 1 October 2026. Board service is voluntary and unpaid, although Directors may have opportunities to represent the CBF at regional and international meetings, convenings and other strategic engagements, including travel where appropriate.

Individuals interested in contributing at a governance level to Caribbean conservation and sustainable development should review the opportunity carefully and submit their expression of interest or nomination before the 7 September 2026 deadline.

For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.

item.content:encoded:
Mission 44 is inviting experienced, passionate and purpose-driven individuals to join its Trustee Board and contribute to an organisation committed to empowering young people and tackling social injustice.

The organisation is currently recruiting Trustee Board Members as part of its efforts to strengthen its leadership and governance while advancing its mission of creating meaningful opportunities and positive change for young people.

This is an opportunity for individuals who have strong professional experience, a commitment to social impact and the ambition to contribute at a board level to an organisation focused on transforming young lives.

The Trustee Board Member position is permanent, hybrid and based in London with remote working options. The role is unremunerated, meaning trustees will not receive a salary for their board service.

The application deadline is September 13, 2026.

About Mission 44

Mission 44 is an organisation focused on empowering young people to overcome social injustice and creating pathways through which young people can achieve their potential.

The organisation brings together a diverse Board, staff team and Youth Advisory Board. This diversity is intended to provide the breadth of perspectives, experiences and ideas needed to drive meaningful and potentially radical change.

Mission 44 says it welcomes applications from all sections of society and is particularly interested in candidates from underrepresented groups.

The organisation is therefore looking for people who combine strong skills and experience with a genuine passion for transforming young lives and a positive, solution-oriented approach to social change.

Mission 44 Trustee Board Members Opportunity

The current vacancy is for Trustee Board Members within Mission 44’s Impact function.

Trustees play an important role in the governance and strategic direction of an organisation. While the information provided does not specify individual trustee responsibilities in detail, the position is part of Mission 44’s leadership and governance structure.

Successful candidates will have the opportunity to contribute their knowledge, professional expertise and perspective to an organisation working to empower young people and address social injustice.

Key details at a glance

  • Organisation: Mission 44
  • Position: Trustee Board Members
  • Category: Leadership and governance opportunity
  • Department/Area: Impact
  • Location: London, United Kingdom, with remote working
  • Working arrangement: Hybrid
  • Contract: Permanent
  • Remuneration: Unremunerated
  • Application deadline: September 13, 2026
  • Application: Through the designated recruitment platform
  • Applicant information: An Applicant Pack is available for candidates

Who Should Apply?

Mission 44 is seeking people who are motivated by social impact and have the skills, experience and commitment necessary to contribute meaningfully to its Board.

The organisation specifically highlights its interest in candidates who can bring diverse perspectives and those from groups that are currently underrepresented.

Potential applicants should, therefore, consider applying if they can demonstrate a strong combination of

  1. Professional expertise relevant to organisational leadership, governance, strategy, impact or related areas.
  2. A commitment to social change, particularly initiatives that improve opportunities and outcomes for young people.
  3. Strong judgement and strategic thinking that can contribute to board-level discussions and decision-making.
  4. A collaborative approach to working with other Board members, staff and young people.
  5. An understanding of diversity and inclusion and the importance of bringing different perspectives into organisational decision-making.
  6. Passion and optimism about creating meaningful and sustainable change.

Mission 44’s recruitment message indicates that it is looking beyond technical qualifications alone. It wants people with a genuine passion for transforming young lives, impressive skills and experience, and the optimism needed to help drive change.

Diversity and Inclusion

One of the notable aspects of this recruitment is Mission 44’s explicit encouragement of applications from across society.

The organisation states that it welcomes applications from all sections of society, while particularly encouraging candidates from underrepresented groups.

This means prospective applicants should not assume that they are excluded simply because they do not fit a traditional profile for board leadership. Instead, candidates should focus on the skills, experience, perspectives and values they can contribute to Mission 44’s mission.

A diverse Board can help an organisation understand the different experiences of the communities it serves, challenge assumptions, improve decision-making, and develop more inclusive approaches to social change.

Location and Working Arrangement

The Trustee Board Member opportunity is advertised as hybrid, with London and remote working options.

This provides flexibility for trustees while maintaining opportunities for engagement with Mission 44’s team and Board activities.

Candidates should carefully review the Applicant Pack and application information to understand any specific expectations concerning attendance, meetings, location or availability.

Is the Mission 44 Trustee Role Paid?

The Trustee Board Member position is listed as unremunerated.

This means candidates should not apply expecting a salary or conventional employment compensation for serving as a trustee.

Instead, the opportunity is primarily suited to individuals who are interested in contributing their expertise, leadership and experience to a social-impact organisation and helping advance its mission.

Applicants should therefore consider the role as a governance and impact opportunity rather than a conventional paid employment position.

Why Consider the Mission 44 Trustee Opportunity?

There are several reasons why experienced professionals may want to consider this opportunity.

1. Contribute to youth empowerment

Mission 44 is focused on empowering young people and helping them overcome social injustice.

Serving on its Board provides an opportunity to contribute to that mission at a strategic level.

2. Use your professional experience for social impact

Individuals with significant experience in areas relevant to governance, strategy, impact, communications, finance, law, fundraising, organisational development or other disciplines may be able to use their expertise to support the organisation’s work.

3. Contribute to strategic leadership

Trustees have an important role in helping organisations maintain strong governance and make sound strategic decisions.

This can provide an opportunity for experienced professionals to contribute beyond their normal organisational responsibilities.

4. Bring a different perspective

Mission 44 is particularly interested in candidates from underrepresented groups.

Individuals with different lived experiences, professional backgrounds and perspectives can help strengthen board-level conversations and contribute to more inclusive decision-making.

5. Support long-term social change

The opportunity offers the chance to contribute to an organisation whose stated goal is to help young people overcome social injustice and create positive change.

For professionals motivated by purpose and social impact, this can be a meaningful way to apply their expertise.

Mission 44 Employee Benefits and Organisational Culture

Although the Trustee Board Member role itself is unremunerated, Mission 44’s careers information highlights a range of benefits available within its broader employment environment.

These benefits provide insight into the organisation’s approach to staff wellbeing, development and work-life balance.

Annual leave

Mission 44 provides employees with 28 days of annual leave, together with an additional day off for their birthday.

The organisation recognises the importance of rest and time away from work as part of maintaining effective performance.

Summer Fridays

During August, Mission 44 finishes work at noon every Friday, giving employees additional time to enjoy the summer period.

Volunteer days

Employees can access unlimited volunteer days, subject to agreement with their manager.

This reflects the organisation’s wider emphasis on social impact and community engagement.

Bike-to-work and gym membership

Mission 44 offers a bike-to-work scheme as well as free gym membership, supporting employees who want to remain active and healthy.

Private health insurance

Employees have access to private health insurance and an employee assistance programme.

Wellbeing allowance

The organisation also provides a wellbeing allowance, which employees can use in a way that works for them.

Pension

Mission 44 provides an employee pension package designed to help employees plan for retirement.

Professional development

Employees receive a professional development budget that can be used for courses and workshops.

This supports continuous learning and career development.

Paid parental leave

Mission 44 provides 37 weeks of paid parental leave, with an option to share the leave with a partner.

How to Apply for the Mission 44 Trustee Board Opportunity

Individuals interested in the Trustee Board Member position should review the official vacancy information and Applicant Pack before submitting an application.

The recruitment listing provides an application route through the designated recruitment platform.

Applicants should make sure they understand the expectations of a trustee position and demonstrate clearly how their professional experience, leadership capabilities, values and perspective could contribute to Mission 44.

A strong application should focus on evidence rather than simply listing qualifications.

Candidates can strengthen their application by explaining the following:

  • Their most relevant professional experience.
  • Leadership or governance experience they have gained.
  • Their understanding of social impact and organisational change.
  • Their experience working collaboratively with diverse stakeholders.
  • The perspective they would bring to the Mission 44 Board.
  • Their motivation for supporting young people and addressing social injustice.
  • Examples of situations where they have demonstrated sound judgement, strategic thinking or leadership.
  • How their skills could complement the existing Board.

APPLY HERE

Important Application Advice

Before applying, prospective candidates should carefully read the Applicant Pack because it contains important information about the Trustee appointment.

Candidates should also pay close attention to the distinction between this opportunity and a conventional job vacancy. The role is permanent and involves a formal position within the organisation’s governance structure, but it is unremunerated.

It is therefore particularly suitable for experienced professionals who are willing to contribute their time and expertise to a social-impact organisation.

Candidates from underrepresented backgrounds are encouraged to consider applying, as Mission 44 has explicitly stated its interest in increasing representation.

Deadline for Application

The deadline to apply for the Mission 44 Trustee Board Members opportunity is

September 13, 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and should avoid waiting until the final day in case additional information or application requirements need to be addressed.

Who Qualifies for This Opportunity?

Category of opportunity: Leadership and governance opportunity / Trustee Board appointment.

Target applicants: Experienced professionals and individuals with relevant skills, experience, leadership capabilities and a strong commitment to social impact and empowering young people.

Academic qualifications: The information provided does not specify a particular academic degree or minimum educational qualification. Candidates should therefore focus on the experience, skills and expertise relevant to the trustee role and consult the Applicant Pack for detailed requirements.

Geographical eligibility: The vacancy is associated with London, United Kingdom, with a hybrid London/remote working arrangement. The provided vacancy information does not state a specific nationality requirement or restrict applications to citizens of a particular country.

Diversity: Mission 44 welcomes applications from all sections of society and has specifically expressed interest in candidates from underrepresented groups.

Visit HERE for more information about the Mission 44 Trustee Board Members Opportunity 2026.

Conclusion

The Mission 44 Trustee Board Members opportunity provides experienced and purpose-driven professionals with an opportunity to contribute to the governance and strategic direction of an organisation committed to empowering young people and tackling social injustice.

While the position is unremunerated, it offers the opportunity to apply professional expertise, leadership experience and diverse perspectives to a social-impact mission. Mission 44’s emphasis on diversity also makes the opportunity particularly relevant to professionals who can bring perspectives that are underrepresented in leadership and governance.

Interested candidates should carefully review the Applicant Pack, assess how their experience aligns with the organisation’s mission and prepare a strong application demonstrating the value they could bring to the Board.

The application deadline is September 13, 2026. Candidates interested in contributing to youth empowerment, social justice and long-term organisational change should consider submitting their applications before the deadline.

For more global Job opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is offering a valuable opportunity for selected nonprofit organizations to transform their existing software and technology projects into publicly accessible, licensed and well-documented open source tools — at no cost to participating organizations. The partnership brings together Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward to support a small group of technology-focused nonprofits with the technical expertise, student developer capacity and industry mentorship needed to prepare software for open source use or strengthen projects that are already part of the open source ecosystem. As part of the program, each selected nonprofit will receive a dedicated team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers who will work on the organization’s project for 16 weeks. The program represents approximately 800 hours of technical work per team, supported by weekly check-ins, technical guidance, project management assistance and team coaching. The program is particularly relevant for nonprofits that have developed useful technology but lack the time, staff capacity or specialised expertise required to properly license, document, package and maintain that technology as an open source resource.

Applications for the program close on September 9, 2026.

Nonprofit Open Source Partnership 2026 at a Glance

  • Program: Nonprofit Open Source Partnership
  • Organizing partners: Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward
  • Target applicants: Selected technology-focused nonprofit organizations
  • Project focus: Open sourcing an existing nonprofit software tool or contributing to an existing open source project
  • Technical support: Eight college student volunteer developers per nonprofit
  • Program duration: 16 weeks
  • Technical contribution: Approximately 800 hours per team
  • Industry mentorship: Bloomberg employee volunteers
  • Open source guidance: CodeDay
  • Program support: Develop for Good
  • Cost: No cost to participating nonprofits
  • Nonprofit application deadline: September 9, 2026
  • Selection notification: October 2, 2026
  • Program kickoff: October 25, 2026
  • Final delivery: February 20, 2027

What Is the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership?

Many nonprofit organizations build or use technology to deliver their missions, but creating software and preparing it for open source distribution are two different challenges.

A nonprofit may have an existing application, platform, internal tool or other technology that could potentially benefit other organizations. However, making that technology genuinely open source involves much more than publishing code online.

The organization may need to address:

  • Software licensing
  • Technical documentation
  • Code organization
  • Developer onboarding
  • Project contribution processes
  • Technical maintenance
  • User documentation
  • Open source best practices
  • Project management
  • Quality assurance
  • Collaboration with external developers

These tasks require time and specialised technical knowledge that many nonprofits may not have available internally.

The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is designed to help close this gap.

Through the partnership, participating organizations receive a dedicated team of student developers and support from experienced professionals who can help turn an existing technology project into a more accessible and reusable open source resource.

Who Is Behind the Program?

The initiative is a collaboration between four organizations:

Bloomberg

Bloomberg is participating in the partnership through employee volunteers who will provide guidance and mentorship to participating nonprofit projects.

Develop for Good

Develop for Good provides the student development teams and program support. The organization will run weekly check-ins with participating students and provide structured support covering technical work, project management and team coaching.

CodeDay

CodeDay will provide guidance on open source best practices, helping participating nonprofits understand how to prepare their projects for open source use.

Fast Forward

Fast Forward is also part of the partnership, contributing to an initiative designed to strengthen technology capacity within the nonprofit sector.

Together, these organizations provide a combination of student technical talent, professional mentorship, open source expertise and program management support.

What Will Selected Nonprofits Receive?

Selected organizations will receive several forms of support throughout the 16-week program.

1. A Dedicated Team of Eight Student Developers

Each participating nonprofit will receive a team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers.

The students will dedicate their time to the nonprofit’s selected project throughout the 16-week program.

This gives nonprofits access to a substantial pool of technical capacity without the financial cost associated with hiring a conventional software development team.

2. Approximately 800 Hours of Technical Work

The program estimates that each team will contribute approximately 800 hours of technical work.

This can provide significant development capacity for a nonprofit that may otherwise struggle to dedicate internal resources to an open source initiative.

The exact nature of the work will depend on the organization’s project and the objectives established for the program.

Potential work could involve preparing an existing tool for open source publication, improving documentation or contributing to an existing open source project.

3. Weekly Program Check-Ins

Develop for Good will conduct weekly check-ins with students throughout the program.

These check-ins are designed to help teams remain focused, address challenges and maintain progress toward the project’s objectives.

4. Technical Support

Participating teams will receive structured technical support to help them move their projects forward.

This can be especially valuable for organizations that have a strong mission and a useful technology product but do not have extensive internal software engineering capacity.

5. Project Management Support

The partnership also includes project management assistance.

This helps keep the work organized and ensures that the student development team and nonprofit point-of-contact remain aligned on priorities, deliverables and timelines.

6. Team Coaching

Teams will receive coaching designed to support effective collaboration and project execution.

Because the program involves nonprofit staff, student developers and industry mentors, structured coaching can help ensure that different participants remain coordinated throughout the 16-week engagement.

7. Open Source Best-Practices Guidance

CodeDay will provide guidance on open source best practices.

This is particularly important for nonprofits that are making the transition from an internally developed or privately maintained tool to a publicly accessible project.

8. Bloomberg Employee Mentorship

Participating nonprofits will receive weekly guidance from experienced Bloomberg employee volunteers.

These mentors are described as being invested in the success of the projects and can provide an additional professional perspective throughout the program.

9. A Publicly Accessible and Documented Final Product

One of the most important outcomes is a finished project that is intended to be:

  • Publicly accessible
  • Properly licensed
  • Documented
  • Ready for the nonprofit to use
  • Potentially useful to other organizations

This can extend the impact of a nonprofit’s technology beyond its immediate internal use.

What Does “Open Source” Mean for Participating Nonprofits?

Open source software is software whose source code is made available under a license that allows others to access, use and, depending on the license, modify and redistribute it under defined conditions.

For a nonprofit, making a tool open source can create opportunities for other organizations, developers and communities to benefit from technology that might otherwise remain limited to the organization that originally developed it.

However, simply uploading software to a public repository does not necessarily mean that a project is ready for meaningful open source collaboration.

A well-prepared open source project generally needs appropriate licensing, clear documentation and enough structure for other users or developers to understand how the project works and how they can engage with it.

That is the gap this partnership is intended to address.

Learn more HERE

What Types of Projects Can Participate?

The program is designed for nonprofits with an existing technology project that is ready to be open sourced or that needs support to contribute to an existing open source project.

A nonprofit may therefore consider applying if it has:

  • An existing software tool it wants to make open source
  • A technology project that needs improved documentation
  • A software project that needs preparation for public release
  • An existing open source project that requires development support
  • A technical project that could benefit from a dedicated student development team

The organization should have a sufficiently defined project for the student developers and mentors to work on during the 16-week program.

Apply HERE

What Does the Nonprofit Need to Contribute?

Although the program is offered at no cost to participating organizations, selected nonprofits are expected to commit time and resources in the form of staff participation.

Each participating nonprofit should plan for approximately:

2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks

from a designated point-of-contact.

The nonprofit point-of-contact will participate in activities such as:

  • Regular check-ins
  • Providing feedback
  • Collaborating with student developers
  • Working with industry mentors
  • Answering project-related questions
  • Helping clarify priorities
  • Reviewing project progress
  • Supporting decision-making when necessary

This commitment is important because the student developers and mentors need a knowledgeable representative from the nonprofit to provide context and feedback.

How Much Time Should a Nonprofit Expect to Commit?

The stated commitment is approximately 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks.

Over the entire program period, this represents approximately 32–48 hours of point-of-contact involvement.

Organizations should therefore select someone who can consistently participate throughout the program.

A nonprofit that cannot provide a reliable point-of-contact may struggle to take full advantage of the technical resources being provided.

What Does the Program Cost?

The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is offered at no cost to participating organizations.

This is one of the program’s major advantages because nonprofits can receive substantial technical support without having to pay for a professional software development team.

The program combines volunteer student developers with industry mentors and structured organizational support to provide the technical capacity needed to advance participating projects.

Why Open Source Can Matter for Nonprofits

Transforming nonprofit software into open source can have benefits beyond the immediate project.

A well-documented and publicly accessible tool can potentially:

  • Allow other nonprofits to use the technology.
  • Encourage collaboration among developers.
  • Reduce duplication of technology development.
  • Create opportunities for external contributions.
  • Increase the visibility of the organization’s technical work.
  • Make the software easier for other organizations to evaluate and adopt.
  • Build a community around a useful technology project.
  • Extend the impact of technology developed for a specific nonprofit mission.

The potential impact depends on the quality of the project, the needs of the wider community and the nonprofit’s ability to maintain and support the software after the program concludes.

Program Timeline

The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership has a defined timeline from application through final delivery.

September 9, 2026 — Applications Close

This is the deadline for nonprofit organizations to submit their applications.

Organizations interested in participating should complete their application before this date.

October 2, 2026 — Selected Nonprofits Notified

Organizations selected to participate will be notified on this date.

October 25, 2026 — Program Kickoff

The program officially begins with the kickoff on October 25, 2026.

This marks the beginning of the 16-week collaboration involving the nonprofit, student developers and mentors.

February 20, 2027 — Final Delivery

The program is scheduled to conclude with final delivery on February 20, 2027.

By this stage, participating teams will have worked toward completing the agreed project objectives.

How to Apply for the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership

Nonprofit organizations interested in participating should submit an application through the program’s online application form.

Application deadline: September 9, 2026.

Apply for the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership

Before applying, organizations should make sure they understand the program requirements and can commit the necessary staff time for the entire 16-week period.

How Nonprofits Can Prepare a Strong Application

Although the provided information does not specify a detailed scoring rubric, organizations can prepare by clearly defining the project they want the program to support.

1. Identify the technology project

Determine which existing tool or project you want the student development team to work on.

The project should be sufficiently defined to explain what the team will be expected to accomplish.

2. Explain why the project should become open source

Organizations should be prepared to explain the value of making their technology publicly accessible.

Consider:

  • Who could benefit from the software?
  • What problem does the tool solve?
  • Why would other organizations use it?
  • What could an open source community contribute?
  • How could open sourcing the project increase its impact?

3. Define the technical challenges

Identify the areas where your organization needs support.

These could include:

  • Software development
  • Documentation
  • Open source preparation
  • Technical improvements
  • Contribution workflows
  • Existing open source development

A clear understanding of the project’s technical needs can help the development team work more effectively.

4. Identify a reliable point-of-contact

Choose a staff member or representative who can commit 2–3 hours each week for 16 weeks.

The person should have enough knowledge of the project to answer questions and provide meaningful feedback.

5. Consider the project’s sustainability

Open sourcing a project is not necessarily the end of the work.

Organizations should consider how the software will be maintained, documented and supported after the partnership ends.

Thinking about sustainability in advance can help ensure that the project’s results remain useful after February 2027.

Who Should Apply?

The opportunity is especially relevant to nonprofit organizations that have an existing technology or software project and want technical assistance to make it open source or contribute to an existing open source project.

A strong potential applicant may be a nonprofit that:

  • Has already built a software tool.
  • Has an existing technology project.
  • Wants to release its software as open source.
  • Needs assistance with documentation.
  • Wants to improve an existing open source project.
  • Has limited internal technical capacity.
  • Can provide a dedicated point-of-contact.
  • Can commit 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks.
  • Is prepared to collaborate closely with student developers and mentors.

What the Program Does Not Provide

Applicants should also understand the nature of the opportunity.

This is not described as a cash grant or direct financial award to nonprofits.

Instead, the core support comes in the form of:

  • Volunteer software development
  • Technical assistance
  • Open source guidance
  • Industry mentorship
  • Project management support
  • Team coaching
  • A structured 16-week development engagement

The primary value is therefore technical capacity and expertise rather than direct funding.

Questions to Ask Before Applying

Before submitting an application, a nonprofit should consider:

  1. Do we have an existing technology project?
  2. Is the project suitable for open source development?
  3. Are we prepared to make the project publicly accessible?
  4. Do we have a clear understanding of what technical work is required?
  5. Can we identify a point-of-contact?
  6. Can that person commit 2–3 hours every week for 16 weeks?
  7. Can our organization provide timely feedback to developers?
  8. Are we prepared to work collaboratively with college student developers?
  9. Can we engage with industry mentors?
  10. Do we have a plan for using or maintaining the project’s output after the program concludes?

If the answer to these questions is generally yes, the partnership may be worth considering.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership?

It is a collaborative program involving Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward that provides selected nonprofits with technical assistance to turn an existing software tool into an open source project or contribute to an existing open source project.

How many student developers does each nonprofit receive?

Each participating nonprofit receives a team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers.

How long does the program last?

The program runs for 16 weeks.

How much technical work is provided?

Each team is expected to contribute approximately 800 hours of technical work.

Does the program charge participating nonprofits?

No. The opportunity is provided at no cost to participating nonprofits.

How much time must the nonprofit contribute?

The nonprofit’s designated point-of-contact should expect to contribute approximately 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks.

What will the nonprofit representative do?

The point-of-contact will participate in check-ins, provide feedback and collaborate with student developers and industry mentors.

Does the program help with open source best practices?

Yes. CodeDay provides guidance on open source best practices.

Will nonprofits receive professional mentorship?

Yes. Experienced Bloomberg employee volunteers provide weekly guidance throughout the program.

What happens at the end of the program?

The program is scheduled to have its final delivery on February 20, 2027.

The intended outcome is a publicly accessible, licensed and documented project that the nonprofit can use and that may potentially be useful to other organizations.

When is the application deadline?

The nonprofit application deadline is September 9, 2026.

How do I apply?

Applications are submitted through the online application form:

Nonprofit Open Source Partnership application form

Contact Information

Organizations with questions about the program can contact:

Michael Gabrielle
Nonprofit Partnerships Manager
Develop for Good

Email: michael@developforgood.org

Important Dates to Remember

For convenience, applicants should keep the following dates in mind:

Date Milestone
September 9, 2026 Nonprofit applications close
October 2, 2026 Selected nonprofits notified
October 25, 2026 Program kickoff
February 20, 2027 Final delivery

The most immediate date for prospective applicants is September 9, 2026, which is the application deadline.

Conclusion

The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership provides selected nonprofits with an opportunity to access significant technical development capacity without paying for it. Through a collaboration involving Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward, participating organizations can receive a dedicated team of eight college student developers, industry mentorship, open source guidance and structured project support.

The program is particularly relevant for nonprofits that have already developed a software tool but lack the internal time or technical capacity needed to properly prepare it for open source use. Rather than simply publishing existing code, participating teams can work toward creating a project that is publicly accessible, appropriately licensed and documented for future use.

The commitment from nonprofits is also clearly defined. Each organization should provide a point-of-contact who can dedicate approximately 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks to check-ins, feedback and collaboration. This involvement will be important for ensuring that student developers understand the organization’s mission, users and technical priorities.

With applications closing on September 9, 2026, eligible nonprofits should begin identifying a suitable project, establishing their technical needs and selecting a reliable point-of-contact as soon as possible.

For nonprofits looking to expand the impact of their technology, improve an existing open source project or make an internally developed tool available to a wider community, this partnership offers an opportunity to gain technical expertise and development support without direct program costs.

Application deadline: September 9, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Key Details

  • Programme: Princeton in Africa Fellowship
  • Fellowship duration: 12 months
  • Location: Various countries across Africa
  • Target group: Young professionals and graduating undergraduates
  • Degree requirement: Bachelor’s, Master’s or PhD
  • English requirement: Professional proficiency at CEFR C1 or above
  • Age limit: Applicants must be no older than 35 during the fellowship year
  • Application fee: None
  • Application deadline: 26 October 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Daylight Time
  • Fellowship period: 2027–2028

Princeton in Africa (PiAf) is a nonprofit organization that offers year-long paid post-graduate fellowship opportunities with a variety of organizations working across the African continent. Fellowships are open to graduates of U.S.-accredited colleges & universities as well as colleges & universities based on the African continent. A list of our current 2026-27 Fellows is here.

Since our launch in 1999, Princeton in Africa has placed over 790 Fellows in 37 countries across the continent. PiAf Fellows work in many different sectors, including international humanitarian aid, public & community health, business & economic development, agricultural development, and education & youth capacity building. Our host organizations include the African Leadership Academy, Baylor College of Medicine Children’s Foundation, Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), Farming Out of Poverty (FOOP), International Rescue Committee, and many other organizations – both large and small – doing remarkable work around the African continent.

The deadline for 2027-28 fellowship applications is Monday, October 26th, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Daylight Time.

*Please note that the “Decision Date” listed on the application is the date by which applicants will be notified of whether or not they will advance to the interview stage of the application cycle.  “Decision Date” refers only to the decision of whether or not an applicant will be invited to interview, not to the final decision of who is accepted to the Princeton in Africa fellowship program. Final fellowship offers will be sent to selected applicants on a rolling basis during our placement period, from February-May 2027. 

How to Apply

The 2027-28 fellowship application is open here!

The deadline for 2027-28 fellowship applications is Monday, Oct. 26th, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Daylight Time.

For information on the 2027-2028 fellowship cycle, please sign up for our applicant mailing list.

Eligibility & Application Requirements

Fellowship Program Eligibility:

To be eligible for the 2027-28 Princeton in Africa Fellowship, all applicants must:

  • Be young professionals or current undergraduates graduating by June 2027 at the time of application.*
  • Hold a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or a Ph.D. from either:
    • A 4-year U.S.-accredited university, or
    • A 4-year locally-accredited university based in Africa
  • Have full professional proficiency in speaking, reading and writing English as defined by the CEFR (Level C1 and above). Additional professional proficiency in Arabic, French, Kiswahili, or Portuguese is preferred for some posts.
  • Be no older than 35 years of age for the duration of the fellowship year (born on or after September 1, 1992).
  • Hold a passport that is valid until at least 6 months after the end of the fellowship year.

* Applicants must not be enrolled in any graduate, doctoral, or equivalent advanced academic programs during their fellowship year.

In 2023-24, Princeton in Africa launched the Nexus Program in order to expand access to our Fellowships and deepen our impact by reaching more young professionals educated and living in Africa. Learn more about the Nexus Program here . Nexus and general applicants will apply using the same process and application portal.

For the 2027-28 cycle, Princeton in Africa is expanding its efforts to connect exceptional emerging leaders with organizations and investors shaping Africa’s growing innovation economy through a targeted Innovation Fellowship program. Applicants who are interested in Innovation Fellowship posts should indicate as such in their application forms.

────────────────────────────────

Application Requirements

To apply, please complete all sections of our online application. Please review the list below for all required components and follow the instructions on the online application carefully. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Additional details can be found in our FAQs page and in the application.

REQUIRED FOR ALL APPLICANTS:

  • Online application questionnaires and essays 
    • Applicants interested in the Innovation Fellowship should complete the supplemental Innovation Fellowship questionnaire found in the application portal. Please see our FAQs for more information.
  • Resume or CV
    • Maximum 2 pages with font size 10 or higher.
    • PDF Format.
  • Official Transcript
    • Must be sent directly from your university to piafapp@princetoninafrica.org via a secure online platform or official university email.
    • Transcripts must be in English (or include an English translation). Additional details available in our FAQs.
  • One Letter of Recommendation
    • Submitted directly by your recommender via form in the online application.

Additional Notes:

  • Princeton in Africa does not confirm receipt of individual materials. Applicants may instead track their application materials through their application portal.
  • Please do not call the PiAf office with application-related questions. Instead, please direct all inquiries to piafapp@princetoninafrica.org.

Policy Updates:

  • Beginning with the 2027-28 Fellowship Application Cycle, all applicants will use the same application forms, regardless of University location or country of residence.
  • Beginning with the 2026-27 Fellowship Application Cycle, applicants will only need to request an official transcript be submitted to piafapp@princetoninafrica.org directly by their university. An unofficial transcript will no longer be required.
  • As of 9/17/22, Princeton in Africa is no longer requiring applicants to pay a $75 non-refundable application fee.

───────────────────────────────

The Princeton in Africa Fellowship Experience

A Princeton in Africa fellowship experience is a one-of-a-kind opportunity for personal and professional development and growth. It is often described as a way to get a foot in the door in key sectors on the African continent. It is also an opportunity to join a growing community of passionate PiAf alumni.

The fellowship experience varies greatly depending on placement and organization. Some Fellows work closely with a supervisor or colleague(s); others work more independently. Some Fellows work in offices that are filled with local staff; others work with a high number of international staff. Some Fellows live in urban areas like Johannesburg and Nairobi; others are based in very rural areas with limited amenities.

All Fellows will be required to attend a pre-departure orientation as well as a mid-year retreat, both of which are designed to foster professional development and community building among the Fellowship cohort.

No matter the host organization or the location, all fellowships are 12 months long and all Fellows are supported by Princeton in Africa staff, alumni, and other Fellows. Community is a PiAf guarantee.

Expenses For The Fellowship

The Princeton in Africa experience is an investment on the part of each Fellow, each fellowship organization, and Princeton in Africa.

Fellows should expect to cover:

  • $350 program placement fee upon acceptance of a fellowship offer.
  • Depending on the post, round-trip airfare to and from their fellowship post in their host country.
  • Pre-departure medical expenses (e.g. immunizations, malaria prevention meds, personal meds, visit for completing medical release form).
  • Depending on the post, Fellows may contribute to visa or work permit costs.
  • Partial cost of travel to mid-year Retreat.

Note: PiAf is committed to ensuring all applicants are able to participate in the program regardless of their financial situation. Once placed with a host organization, a financial aid application is available to Fellows with demonstrated need. Fellows with demonstrated need can ask questions about the process to PiAf staff.

Princeton in Africa/Fellowship Organizations cover*:

  • Housing and living stipend.
  • Certain visas/work permits.
  • Medical insurance, medical evacuation insurance, security evacuation insurance.
  • Mid-year Retreat with meals, housing, and activities, and partial travel allowance.

*Fellowship packages vary post-to-post; details will be provided in the offer letter prior to a Fellow’s acceptance.

Note: Fellowship stipends are intended to cover living costs directly related to the fellowship. Stipends are not meant to cover outside costs, including costs in Fellows’ home countries.

Learn More about Princeton in Africa

Consult these resources for more information about Princeton in Africa:

  • Current Host Organizations
  • Current Fellows
  • Fellows Report Database – provides detailed information about past fellowship experiences. Gain access by emailing piafapp@princetoninafrica.org.
  • Nexus Program – learn more about the Nexus program for graduates of African universities, launched in 2023.
  • PiAf Placement Process Infographic – learn more about our placement process and timeline.

Application & Fellowship Timeline:

Princeton in Africa Fellowship 2027–28 Timeline

Date Application Stage
26 August 2026 Fellowship application opens
16 September 2026 Information session for prospective applicants
26 October 2026 Application deadline
Early December 2026 Applicants notified about interviews
6–12 January 2027 Virtual fellowship interviews
February–May 2027 Acceptance and placement period
4–6 June 2027 Mandatory virtual orientation
9 June–10 August 2027 Fellowships begin
8 June–9 August 2028 Fellowships end

The fellowship application opens on 26 August 2026 and the application deadline is 26 October 2026. Fellowship interviews are scheduled for January 2027, followed by placements between February and May 2027.

Where Can Princeton in Africa Fellows Work?

Fellowship placements vary from year to year and are hosted by organisations working across different sectors and African countries.

Potential areas of work include:

  • International development
  • Humanitarian assistance
  • Public health
  • Community health
  • Education
  • Youth development
  • Agriculture
  • Economic development
  • Business
  • Innovation
  • Community development

The specific fellowship organisations and available positions depend on the fellowship cycle.

Is There an Application Fee?

No.

Princeton in Africa no longer requires applicants to pay the former $75 non-refundable application fee.

Why Apply for the Princeton in Africa Fellowship?

The Princeton in Africa Fellowship can provide young professionals with an opportunity to:

  • Gain 12 months of professional experience in Africa
  • Work with established development and nonprofit organisations
  • Build an international professional network
  • Develop practical skills in their chosen sector
  • Contribute to projects addressing development challenges
  • Connect with a community of PiAf Fellows and alumni
  • Explore career opportunities across the African continent.

The fellowship is also described by Princeton in Africa as an opportunity for personal and professional development and a potential entry point into key sectors across Africa.

Important Note for Applicants

The fellowship experience differs considerably depending on the host organisation and location. Applicants should therefore be prepared to work in different environments, including urban and rural settings.

Applicants should also review Princeton in Africa’s travel, health and safety policies before accepting a placement. The programme has specific travel restrictions and safety requirements for Fellows, including restrictions relating to certain countries and regions.

Apply for the Princeton in Africa Fellowship

If you meet the eligibility requirements and are interested in gaining professional experience through a paid fellowship in Africa, consider applying for the Princeton in Africa Fellowship 2027–28.

Application deadline: 26 October 2026 at 11:59 PM EDT

👉 APPLY NOW: https://gps.princeton.edu/_portal/tds-program-brochure?programid=13573

For additional information, applicants should consult Princeton in Africa’s How to Apply and Frequently Asked Questions resources.

Questions?

For more information about our application cycle timeline and placement process, please visit the How to Apply section of our website and consult our Frequently Asked Questions page.

Application Instructions: Select the link for “apply now”. The link will open the login page. Select the link under the login buttons for “create account”. Complete the User registration form. Note the email address you use to create the account. This will be your username.

If you encounter issues in the application portal, please see our Frequently Asked Questions page for tips on troubleshooting common problems.
