PhD Round 2: Applicants Seeking Doctoral Enrolment

PhD Round 2 is intended for candidates who are not necessarily enrolled in a doctoral programme but are eligible and willing to register at an ACT-PREP partner university.

These applicants must commit to completing their doctoral training within three years.

PhD Round 2 Eligibility

Applicants should:

  • Be nationals of an ACT-PREP partner country.
  • Hold a relevant master’s degree or equivalent.
  • Have a suitable academic background in health, biomedical sciences, public health or a related field.
  • Be eligible to register for a relevant doctoral programme at an ACT-PREP partner university.
  • Propose work under one of the seven priority themes.
  • Secure institutional endorsement.
  • Identify an appropriate host institution and mentor.
  • Provide two referees.
  • Commit to completing doctoral training within three years.

Applicants affiliated with an ACT-PREP institution, including eligible junior researchers, will receive priority consideration.

PhD Round 2 Support

The fellowship may provide:

  • Tuition and university fees.
  • A monthly stipend.
  • A one-time research or clinical-trial grant.
  • Mentorship from ACT-PREP experts.
  • Core and specialized training courses.
  • Access to research sites and datasets.
  • Professional networking.
  • Alumni and mentorship opportunities.

The fellowship can be supported for up to three years, subject to programme and institutional requirements.

Postdoctoral Research Fellowships

The ten postdoctoral positions are designed to help early-career African researchers develop independent research leadership in clinical trials and epidemic preparedness.

Selected researchers will join ongoing ACT-PREP research activities while developing and leading their own research outputs.

Their work must either:

  • Integrate appropriate clinical-trial methodologies; or
  • Address a substantive epidemic preparedness and response topic.

Postdoctoral researchers will be expected to uphold high standards of research quality, ethics and integrity.

Postdoctoral Eligibility

Applicants must:

  • Be nationals of an eligible ACT-PREP country.
  • Hold a PhD in a relevant health, biomedical or related field.
  • Have obtained the PhD within the past five years.
  • Demonstrate a research record appropriate to their postdoctoral career stage.
  • Propose research aligned with an ACT-PREP priority theme.
  • Confirm an appropriate host institution.
  • Obtain endorsement from the home or host institution.
  • Identify a suitable mentor.
  • Provide two referees.
  • Demonstrate potential for research leadership and scientific independence.
  • Submit a complete application before the deadline.

Postdoctoral Support

Selected postdoctoral researchers may receive:

  • A mentored position at a consortium partner institution.
  • A monthly stipend.
  • Research support.
  • Mobility support.
  • Funding for up to 12 months.
  • Training in scientific writing.
  • Training in research leadership.
  • Training in grant administration.
  • Specialized methodological training.
  • Exposure to modelling, bioinformatics and real-world evidence methods.
  • Support to publish research.
  • Support to present findings at conferences.
  • Guidance on securing follow-on research funding.
  • Mentorship from local and international experts.

The call does not specify the stipend, research-support or mobility-support amounts.

4. Research Concept Note

Applicants must prepare a research concept of approximately two to three pages.

It should include:

  • Working research title.
  • Selected ACT-PREP priority theme.
  • Background and rationale.
  • Research problem.
  • Objectives.

5. Motivation Letter

The motivation letter should explain:

  • Why the applicant is interested in ACT-PREP.
  • How the opportunity relates to the applicant’s career.
  • The applicant’s relevant academic and research experience.
  • Why the selected research theme is important.
  • How the applicant will contribute to the consortium.
  • The applicant’s commitment to research quality and integrity.
  • How the applicant intends to strengthen research and epidemic preparedness in Africa.
  • The applicant’s intention to remain connected to and contribute to the region.

6. Institutional Endorsement Letter

An institutional endorsement or nomination letter is mandatory for both PhD and postdoctoral applicants.

It should be prepared on the nominating institution’s official letterhead and confirm:

  • The candidate’s status as a staff member, registered researcher or person eligible to enrol.
  • The institution’s formal support for the application.
  • Alignment of the proposed work with institutional priorities.
  • Willingness to host and support the fellow.
  • Availability of mentorship.
  • Support for enrolment where applicable.
  • Permission to participate in ACT-PREP training and research activities.
  • Institutional support throughout the fellowship period.

7. Two References

Applicants must identify two referees. The application checklist also requires two reference letters.

Referees should comment on:

  • How long they have known the applicant.
  • The capacity in which they know the applicant.
  • The applicant’s research ability.
  • Research independence.
  • Suitability for the fellowship.
  • Potential for research leadership.
  • Likelihood of timely completion.
  • Motivation.
  • Integrity.
  • Teamwork.

The official guidance instructs referees to submit their recommendations directly to the recruitment email by the applicable deadline. Applicants should therefore contact referees early and confirm that their letters have been sent.

Selection Process

Applications will undergo a competitive, multi-stage selection process.

Stage 1: Application Screening

The selection team will verify:

  • Completeness.
  • Eligible nationality.
  • Required academic qualification.
  • Programme enrolment or registration eligibility.
  • Institutional endorsement.
  • Presence of two referees.
  • Research-theme alignment.
  • Submission by the deadline.

Incomplete or ineligible applications may not proceed.

Stage 2: Scientific Evaluation

Eligible applications will undergo scientific review.

Reviewers will assess:

  • Quality of the research concept.
  • Scientific merit.
  • Relevance.
  • Feasibility.
  • Alignment with ACT-PREP themes.
  • Alignment with EDCTP priorities.
  • Potential contribution to clinical trials or epidemic preparedness.
  • Likely scientific or public-health impact.
  • Suitability of the work plan.

Stage 3: Interviews

Shortlisted applicants will be invited to an interview to evaluate:

  • Academic and research readiness.
  • Understanding of the proposed research.
  • Motivation.
  • Communication.
  • Suitability for the fellowship.
  • Ability to complete the research within the available time.
  • Potential for research leadership.
  • Fit with the proposed host and mentor.

Stage 4: Notification

Successful candidates will receive formal notification following the selection process.

Stage 5: Fellowship Commencement

Selected candidates will receive further instructions concerning:

  • Fellowship start date.
  • University enrolment.
  • Host-institution arrangements.
  • Mentorship.
  • Financial arrangements.
  • Training requirements.
  • Onboarding.

A detailed selection schedule will be communicated to shortlisted candidates.

How Applications Will Be Scored

Eligible applications will be evaluated according to:

  • Academic record.
  • Research experience appropriate to the applicant’s career stage.
  • Quality of the proposed research.
  • Feasibility of completing the work.
  • Relevance to clinical trials or epidemic preparedness.
  • Alignment with EDCTP research priorities.
  • Research capability.
  • Potential for leadership and scientific independence.
  • Suitability of the host institution.
  • Suitability of the proposed mentor.
  • Likelihood of timely completion.
  • Quality of motivation.
  • Commitment to contribute to the region.
  • Contribution to the consortium’s equity objectives.
  • Gender balance.
  • Equitable representation across partner countries.

Where two candidates receive equivalent scores, preference may be given to the underrepresented gender and to achieving equitable representation among ACT-PREP partner countries.

Qualified women are strongly encouraged to apply.

Practical Tips for a Competitive Application

  1. Choose the correct fellowship route

    Currently enrolled doctoral researchers should apply under Round 1. Candidates seeking admission to a doctoral programme should use Round 2.

  2. Confirm nationality before applying

    The current call is restricted to nationals of the seven listed ACT-PREP countries.

  3. Secure institutional endorsement early

    The endorsement is mandatory and may require approval from senior university or institutional officials.

  4. Identify a credible host and mentor

    The strength of the host arrangement and the likelihood of timely completion are part of the selection criteria.

  5. Align the concept with one priority theme

    Avoid presenting a general public-health topic without showing its direct connection to ACT-PREP and clinical-trial or epidemic-response priorities.

  6. Develop a realistic work plan

    The project must be achievable within three years for PhD applicants and 12 months for postdoctoral applicants.

  7. Explain the regional value of the research

    Show how the work will strengthen African research systems, institutions, policy, outbreak readiness or clinical-trial capacity.

  8. Demonstrate research integrity

    Address ethical practice, responsible data management and the protection of research participants where relevant.

  9. Use measurable objectives

    Ensure that each objective can be linked to a method, output and realistic timeline.

  10. Contact referees immediately

    Reference letters must be sent directly by the referees before the deadline.

  11. Include publications where applicable

    Postdoctoral applicants should present a research record appropriate to their career stage.

  12. Submit before the final day

    Early submission provides time to correct missing documents or email-delivery problems.

Conclusion

The ACT-PREP PhD and Postdoctoral Research Fellowships provide an important opportunity for African researchers to develop expertise in clinical trials, disease surveillance, artificial intelligence, ethics, regulation, laboratory science, One Health, health-systems resilience and epidemic response.

Through academic funding, stipends, research support, specialized training, mentorship and access to a multi-country research network, the programme aims to prepare a new generation of African researchers to lead high-quality research before, during and after disease outbreaks.

Applicants must select the appropriate fellowship category, establish strong alignment with one of the seven priority themes, secure institutional endorsement and prepare a focused research concept that can be completed within the specified period.

PhD Round 1 applications must be submitted by September 15, 2026, while PhD Round 2 and postdoctoral applications must be submitted by September 30, 2026.
